description: A chief risk officer must decide whether to approve a bank's proposed embedded-finance partnership and finalize the exposure cap, loss reserve, monitoring controls, termination right, and credit support, with input from model risk, compliance, legal, and relationship management.

shared_context.S1: The bank is considering an embedded-finance partnership with Northstar Payments, which would allow Northstar's business customers to draw short-term working-capital advances through the bank's platform.
shared_context.S2: Northstar has requested an initial bank exposure of $5,000,000 for the program.
shared_context.S3: The current draft describes the commercial opportunity and projected fee income but does not set a final exposure cap, reserve amount, monitoring schedule, termination right, or credit-support requirement.
shared_context.S4: Nadia makes the binding risk-approval decision.
shared_context.S5: The bank's normal pre-approval routine is a roundtable in which model risk, compliance, legal, and relationship management each report any findings before Nadia records the final terms.

PF1.text: Elias completed the partner-loss validation this week and found that the program's risk profile requires a maximum bank exposure of exactly $3,000,000 and a loss reserve of exactly $1,800,000; he put the figures in his working paper but it has not yet been attached to the approval file.

PF2.text: Mei received a compliance memo this morning confirming that Northstar's transaction flow requires a monthly enhanced-AML transaction-file review as a condition of approval; the memo has not yet been added to the partnership checklist.

PF3.text: Jonas found while reviewing the draft agreement this week that the bank must have a contractual right to terminate the program on exactly 30 days' notice; he marked the clause in his copy but has not circulated the redline.

PF4.text: Ruth confirmed with Northstar yesterday that its parent company will provide an unconditional $500,000 guarantee for the program, but the signed term sheet has not yet been uploaded to the credit file.

acceptance_conditions: The partnership must be approved with a maximum bank exposure of exactly $3,000,000.
A loss reserve of exactly $1,800,000 must be recorded.
Enhanced AML transaction-file review must be required monthly.
The agreement must provide a termination right on exactly 30 days' notice.
An unconditional parent guarantee of exactly $500,000 must be documented.

content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'Elias' and c['type'] in ['documentation', 'document_upload', 'upload', 'file_upload'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['target'] == 'Mei' and c['type'] in ['documentation', 'document_upload', 'checklist_update', 'upload'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['target'] == 'Jonas' and c['type'] in ['documentation', 'document_upload', 'document_circulation', 'circulation', 'upload'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['target'] == 'Ruth' and c['type'] in ['documentation', 'document_upload', 'document_receipt', 'upload', 'receipt'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft requests $5,000,000 and specifies no reserve; PF1 changes maximum_bank_exposure_usd to exactly $3,000,000, loss_reserve_usd to exactly $1,800,000, and requires Elias's exposure-and-reserve documentation commitment.
The draft has no AML review frequency; PF2 changes enhanced_aml_review_frequency to exactly monthly and requires Mei's checklist-update commitment.
The draft has no termination right; PF3 changes termination_notice_days to exactly 30 and requires Jonas's redline-circulation or document commitment.

The requested exposure has no documented credit support and would not support approval on the draft terms; PF4 changes parent_guarantee_usd to exactly $500,000 and makes conditional approval feasible with Ruth's guarantee-documentation commitment.
